01 The situation

Yamaha holds roughly 70% of branded musical instrument listings on Nigeria’s largest marketplace, and none of them is a Yamaha channel.

There are two routes to a Yamaha in Nigeria today, and they behave very differently.

Route A

The authorised route

The customer identifies an appointed dealer, then contacts them: by phone, WhatsApp, or in person. Pricing is not published. A conversation follows. Then a quote. Then, often, a negotiation.

Route B

The informal route

The customer opens Jiji or Instagram, sees the price immediately, messages the seller, and receives a reply within minutes.

Both routes frequently sell a genuine Yamaha. Only one of them is easy.

The situation · 02 Next · The opportunity

02 The opportunity

The demand already exists.

Walk into a church in Lagos on a Sunday, a studio in Surulere, a school hall in Abuja. Yamaha is already in the room, and has been for decades. We are not building awareness. We are building capture.

Four things stand between existing demand and completed transactions.

01

No visible price.

The single largest friction point, and the one the informal channel exploits.

02

No transactional route.

No authorised path from browsing to owning without human intervention.

03

No verification.

No way for a buyer to confirm that what they are buying is genuine and supported.

04

No Nigerian brand presence.

No dedicated national channel. Official Yamaha social covers the entire African continent from one account.

One outcome. Two connected systems.

A

Visibility.

Yamaha Music discoverable, consistent and preferred across Nigerian and West African touchpoints.

Confidence
B

Commerce.

A route to purchase that is findable, priced, trusted and deliverable.

Visibility earns attention. Confidence turns it into action.

Overview · 05 Next · Part I · Strategic approach

I · 01 Strategic approach

Positioning

For everyone in West Africa who makes sound: the worship team, the producer, the touring band, the teacher, the parent buying a first keyboard. Yamaha is the instrument you can buy with certainty.

Where the market offers a gamble dressed as a bargain, Yamaha offers what no informal seller can: the assurance that what you bought is what you will still be playing in ten years.

Five commitments. Not adjectives.

We claim
Requires
Authorised
Clear, verifiable identification as an appointed channel.
Warranted
Warranty registrable and honourable in-region.
Serviceable
Parts, tuning and repair reachable locally.
Honestly priced
Naira pricing, published or reliably quotable.
Within reach
Findable, deliverable, installable.
Strategic approach · I · 01 Next · Audiences & messaging

I · 02 Audiences & messaging

Seven segments.Three carry the weight.

Content and media weight to three priority segments: producers first, then working musicians, then worship teams. Four further segments carry secondary investment.

Priority segment 01

Producers & studios.

Buying

Accuracy and translation. Spec-literate, comparison-heavy.

Message

Hear it the way the world will hear it. Reference-standard monitoring and capture: what the records you admire were made on.

Proof

Technical spec · studio credits · Nigerian producers on record · A/B demonstration content.

Priority segment 02

Working musicians & artists.

Buying

Feel, stage reliability, peer credibility.

Message

It will not let you down in front of people. Made to survive the road. The action and tone you already know, serviced between tours and not shipped abroad.

Proof

Artist usage · road-durability content · backline presence at Nigerian venues.

Priority segment 03

Worship teams & churches.

Buying

Reliability under weekly, heavy, non-expert use. Committee decision, budget-constrained.

Message

The instrument that will still be right in ten years of Sundays. Serviceable here, by people you can reach. One purchase instead of three replacements.

Proof

Durability record · local service capability · warranty terms · Nigerian churches already using Yamaha.

Four secondary segments · secondary investment

Schools & music education

Instruments that outlast the students. Education range, institutional warranty, Yamaha’s global music-education heritage.

Venues, theatres & install

Specified once, supported for the life of the room. Professional audio, install references, project support model.

Home & lifestyle

The instrument that belongs in the room even when nobody is playing. Digital pianos, home audio, silent practice.

Parents & first instruments

Start them on something that will not put them off. Entry range and pricing, learning features, progression pathway.

Audiences · I · 02 Next · Channels & cadence

I · 03 Channels & cadence

Seven channels. One voice.

Each channel earns a role. None is run for its own sake, and none duplicates another. The site carries search and conversion, so it takes the heaviest weight.

Instagram Primary brand and community channel. The daily face of Yamaha to musicians, producers and buyers.
TikTok Reach and demonstration. Younger players, students, and the discovery audience.
Facebook Church, institutional and older buyer segments, where the committee purchase begins.
YouTube Long-form and demonstration. Brand film, tutorials, and the searches that precede a considered purchase.
X Producer and industry conversation. Presence where the professional debate happens.
Email Lead nurture, the consultative pipeline, and the relationship after purchase.
Site & SEOHeaviest weight Buy Right content, category and product pages. The only channel serving search visibility and conversion at once.
Channels & cadence · I · 03 Next · Team & phasing

I · 04 Team & phasing

A marketing function that does not exist yet.

Yamaha is not buying a campaign. It is buying an operation that runs after the launch noise fades. Seven roles hold it.

01 Account & brand lead Owns the strategy end to end. Holds the standard between Yamaha, its distributors and the work.
02 Community & social manager Builds the audience that gets converted. The brand’s daily voice to musicians, producers and buyers.
03 Content writer Holds the tone of voice consistent across every touchpoint the market meets.
04 Graphic & motion designer Applies the identity system across every channel without loss of coherence.
05 Performance & media buyer Turns strategy into measurable reach. Buys demand capture where the audience already is.
06 Web & technical maintenance Keeps the commerce platform live, fast and safe. Nothing the reader sees breaks.
07 Analytics & reporting Turns activity into evidence: the defensible case for renewal and escalation.

Twelve weeks to first evidence. Six months to extension.

Phase 1

Weeks 1 to 4

Foundation

Audit and baseline complete. Brand platform approved. Catalogue, pricing and stock structured. Platform build underway. Team in place.

Phase 2

Weeks 5 to 8

Launch

Platform live with commerce. Campaign Wave 1 across paid, outdoor and partnerships. Always-on content begins. First monthly report.

Phase 3

Weeks 9 to 12

Scale

Optimised against cost-per-acquisition and share-of-voice. Second asset block. Brand film. Campaign Wave 2. Renewal case.

Phase 4

Months 4 to 6

Extension

Category expansion. Regional reach subject to territory rights. Retail and venue partnership programme scaled.

II · 01 Visual identity direction

Certainty, made visible.

The look takes its cue from the tone of voice: certainty over volume, restraint over decoration, warmth in the human moments and precision in the product ones. It sits inside Yamaha’s global identity, not beside it.

Art direction

Editorial restraint. Instruments in real Nigerian rooms, not studio isolation. Craft detail over lifestyle abstraction.

Colour behaviour

The platform · II · 02 Next · Campaign expression

II · 03 Campaign expression

Every wave starts here.

One line, three ways to prove it. Each key visual takes the same idea from a different entry point, so the campaign can run for a year without repeating itself.

Meaning 01 · Product-led

The instrument comes first.

Before there is a wave, there is the thing you played it on. The instrument in a Nigerian creative room, the room quieter than the instrument.

Meaning 02 · Cultural

West Africa is where waves start.

A Nigerian artist, worship team or producer with a Yamaha instrument, treated with editorial restraint. Nigerian in rhythm, global in standard.

Meaning 03 · Accessibility

You start here.

A beginner with an entry-level Yamaha, shot with the same craft as the professional. A first note is the same promise as a world tour.

Campaign expression · II · 03 Next · Out-of-home & environmental

II · 04 Out-of-home & environmental

From a phone screen to Third Mainland Bridge.

The same system holds at arm’s length and at fifty metres. Two applications show the range: large-format outdoor in Lagos, and the brand inside the rooms where the instruments are actually played.

Large-format outdoor

Lagos: the Ikoyi, Victoria Island or Third Mainland corridor. The campaign line at scale, where the city already looks up.

Interior application

Church, studio, venue or retail. The brand where the buying decision is made and the instrument is used.

Detailed schedule · III · 02 Next · Terms & assumptions

III · 03 Terms & assumptions

Stated honestly.

Six things we need, the assumptions the pricing rests on, and the commercial terms. Anything not listed in the Bill of Quantities is out of scope and quoted separately.

Six things we need from you

01Scope of authority

Territory, categories and channels covered, and who holds final brand approval.

02Service & repair capability

What exists locally today, where, and with what turnaround.

03Pricing policy

Whether naira pricing can be published and held; if not, what mechanism works.

04Product catalogue

SKUs, categories, current pricing, stock visibility and existing systems.

05Grey market estimate

Your own read of parallel import volume in the territory.

06Budget structure

Whether co‑op or market development funds are available.

Assumptions & exclusions

Brand approval stays within the Phase 1 window.

Catalogue and stock data are available at the required detail.

Service capability meets the promises made in the positioning.

Pricing policy permits publication, or a defensible mechanism.

Territory rights permit regional expansion in Phase 4.

Anything not in the Bill of Quantities is out of scope, quoted separately.
